s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive extraocular muscle limitation with a localized orbital mass
salient_findings: Slowly developing limitation in right-eye movement
Restricted abduction of the right eye
Extraconal mass at the right superolateral orbital wall with smooth bone remodeling
key_facts: 5-year-old boy with no prior medical history
No pain, inflammation, fever, trauma, or history of ocular infection
Overall health unchanged
Abduction of the right eye was restricted
No signs of proptosis, strabismus, visual impairment, or inflammation in either eye
Laboratory studies, including an infectious work-up, were negative
Noncontrast CT showed a well-circumscribed extraconal mass at the right superolateral orbital wall
MRI demonstrated a cystic mass in the right superior extraconal compartment
Mild compression on the external and superior rectus muscles
No involvement of the optic nerve, intraconal fat, or intracranial extension

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass with smooth bone remodeling and fluid-attenuating content on imaging

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass with hyperintense signal on T2-weighted images and no internal enhancement

shortlist.label: Orbital lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass in the extraconal compartment with mild compression on surrounding muscles

shortlist.label: Cavernous hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-circumscribed mass with smooth bone remodeling and no signs of aggression

shortlist.label: Colobomatous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass in the orbital region with possible connection to the eye's developmental anomalies

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-circumscribed extraconal mass with smooth bone remodeling and fluid-attenuating content on CT, along with the cystic appearance on MRI that is hyperintense on T2-weighted images and hypointense on FLAIR imaging, is consistent with a dermoid cyst. The location at the orbital wall adjacent to the frontozygomatic suture is also typical for dermoid cysts.

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: While similar to dermoid cysts, epidermoid cysts are less common in this location and typically do not have the same characteristic imaging features.

rejected.label: Orbital lymphangioma
rejected.why: Lymphangiomas are more likely to have a complex, multicystic appearance on imaging and may involve the intraconal space, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Cavernous hemangioma
rejected.why: Cavernous hemangiomas are typically intraconal, show a more heterogeneous appearance on MRI due to blood products, and are less likely to cause bone remodeling.

rejected.label: Colobomatous cyst
rejected.why: Colobomatous cysts are associated with colobomas of the eye and are not typically found in the extraconal space or associated with the imaging characteristics described.
